title: Enhanced Esophageal Cancer Detection Using Spectrum-Aided Vision Enhancer: A Comparative Study of White Light Imaging, Narrow-Band Imaging, and Algorithmic Narrow-Band Imaging-Like Imaging

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Enhanced Esophageal Cancer Detection Using Spectrum-Aided Vision Enhancer: A Comparative Study of White Light Imaging, Narrow-Band Imaging, and Algorithmic Narrow-Band Imaging-Like Imaging》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Background and aims · abstract-1-1】Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) detection is crucial for improving survival. While narrow-band imaging (NBI) improves mucosal visualization, limitations remain. We evaluated the diagnostic performance of the Spectrum-Aided Vision Enhancer (SAVE), an algorithmic NBI-like technology reconstructed from white light imaging (WLI).

【Introduction · deo270467-sec-0050-p1】Esophageal cancer (EC) has emerged as a formidable global health challenge, accounting for approximately 604,100 new diagnoses and 544,076 deaths in 2020 alone, making it a leading cause of oncological mortality worldwide [1, 2, 3]. In high‐incidence regions, such as East Asia and Eastern Africa, esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains the predominant histological subtype [4]. The clinical significance of early detection is profound; when diagnosed and treated at an early stage, the 5‐year survival rate for EC can reach approximately 90% [1]. However, EC often presents with vague symptoms, leading to late diagnosis. The 5‐year survival rate drops sharply to about 47% at the localized stage and only 5% at the advanced stage [5]. This underscores the critical importance of developing advanced diagnostic tools [4].

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Enhanced Esophageal Cancer Detection Using Spectrum-Aided Vision Enhancer: A Comparative Study of White Light Imaging, Narrow-Band Imaging, and Algorithmic Narrow-Band Imaging-Like Imaging》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Dataset and Image Cohort · deo270467-sec-0070-p1】This research was designed as a pre‐clinical, retrospective, image‐based feasibility study. The evaluation used a curated dataset of 1350 still endoscopic images, equally partitioned into 450 images for each imaging modality (WLI, NBI, and SAVE). Within each modality, images were stratified across three clinical stages: normal mucosa, ESD, and ESCC (150 images per stage). The image cohort was derived from 158 patients, including 49 healthy controls, 56 patients with esophageal dysplasia, and 53 with ESCC. All primary WLI and NBI images were acquired using a high‐definition Olympus CV‐290 endoscopy system (Osaka, Japan) at Kaohsiung Medical University Chung‐Ho Memorial Hospital.

【Study Design and Ethical Considerations · deo270467-sec-0090-p1】The study protocol adhered to the ethical principles of the 1964 Declaration of Helsinki and was approved by the Institutional Review Boards of Kaohsiung Medical University Chung‐Ho Memorial Hospital (KMUHIRB‐E(I)‐20230211; May 18, 2023) and National Taiwan University Hospital (No. 202301103RIND; February 15, 2024). Due to the retrospective, anonymized design, the requirement for written informed consent was waived. Multiple images from the same patient were analyzed as independent observations, and no dataset partitioning into training, validation, or testing subsets was performed.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Enhanced Esophageal Cancer Detection Using Spectrum-Aided Vision Enhancer: A Comparative Study of White Light Imaging, Narrow-Band Imaging, and Algorithmic Narrow-Band Imaging-Like Imaging》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion · deo270467-sec-0170-p1】In conclusion, this retrospective exploratory study demonstrates the technical feasibility of using the software‐based SAVE algorithm to reconstruct NBI‐like contrast from conventional WLI images. Descriptively, SAVE showed diagnostic potential for ESCC, with observed diagnostic performance metrics numerically similar to those of established imaging modalities in this exploratory dataset. However, its lower sensitivity for detecting squamous dysplasia represents a significant clinical limitation in its current form. These findings are hypothesis‐generating and support further prospective, patient‐level, multicenter trials to refine the algorithmic spectral reconstruction and evaluate its integration into clinical workflows.

【Results · abstract-3-1】For ESCC, SAVE demonstrated diagnostic performance metrics (sensitivity: 0.81-0.97, specificity: 0.85-0.96) that were numerically similar to WLI and NBI. For dysplasia detection, SAVE had lower observed sensitivity (0.39-0.62) compared to NBI (0.55-0.85) across all observers, representing a clinical limitation for precancerous screening in its current format. Mean per-image reading times were similar across WLI, NBI, and SAVE.

However, its lower sensitivity for detecting squamous dysplasia represents a significant clinical limitation in its current form. These findings are hypothesis‐generating and support further prospective, patient‐level, multicenter trials to refine the algorithmic spectral reconstruction and evaluate its integration into clinical workflows.

For ESCC, SAVE demonstrated diagnostic performance metrics (sensitivity: 0.81-0.97, specificity: 0.85-0.96) that were numerically similar to WLI and NBI. For dysplasia detection, SAVE had lower observed sensitivity (0.39-0.62) compared to NBI (0.55-0.85) across all observers, representing a clinical limitation for precancerous screening in its current format. sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Enhanced Esophageal Cancer Detection Using Spectrum-Aided Vision Enhancer: A Comparative Study of White Light Imaging, Narrow-Band Imaging, and Algorithmic Narrow-Band Imaging-Like Imaging》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【FIGURE 1 · deo270467-fig-0001】FIGURE 1 Experimental flowchart. (A) Model training: WLI images are first color‐corrected and illumination‐compensated, converted to the CIE 1931 XYZ space, and calibrated via the correction matrix [C] using [XYZSpectrum] × pinv([V]). Principal components are extracted by PCA, and a regression‐derived transform [M] is obtained to compute [XYZCorrect] = [C] × [V], accounting for nonlinear response and dark current. A computational RGB‐to‐spectral estimation step is then applied using the regression‐derived transform [M], followed by per‐pixel estimation of spectral reflectance over the 380–780 nm range. Band selection emphasizes hemoglobin absorption regions (∼450 and ∼540 nm). Spectral shape calibration against Olympus narrow‐band imaging (NBI) is optimized using the Macbeth Color Checker and Cauchy–Lorentz modeling with dual annealing, while SSIM, entropy, and PSNR guide denoising and fidelity. (B) Model and physician evaluation: The finalized Spectrum‐Aided Vision Enhancer (SAVE) images, together with original white‐light imaging (WLI) and NBI (450 images per modality; 150 per class: normal, dysplasia, ESCC), are blindly reviewed by three endoscopists with different experience levels (3, 5, and 15 years). Using pathology/clinical standards as reference, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, PPV, NPV, and per‐image reading time are computed across modalities and stages, with inter‐observer comparisons to assess robustness and clinical utility. (Note: A detailed description of the SAVE method is provided in Material S1).
